message.content:
洛杉磯（Pacific Time）與柏林（Central European Time）之間的標準時差為 **9 小時**，即柏林時間比洛杉磯時間快 9 小時。

> **注意：**  
> 兩地都實行夏令時間，但開始與結束日期略有不同。  
> - 在美國夏令時間開始（第二個星期日）到歐洲夏令時間開始（最後一個星期日）之間，洛杉磯已進入夏令時間（UTC‑7），但柏林仍在標準時間（UTC+1），此期間差距縮短至 **8 小時**。  
> - 同理，在歐洲夏令時間結束（最後一個星期日）到美國夏令時間結束（第一個星期日）之間，差距也會縮短至 8 小時。  
> 其餘時間則恢復為 9 小時差。

如果你需要查詢某一天具體的時差，請告訴我那天的日期，我可以幫你算出當時的差距。

The user asks: "洛杉磯和柏林之間的時差是多少？" (What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?). We need to provide the answer. Possibly we might need to use the function to fetch coordinates? But the question is about time difference. We can compute based on time zones: Los Angeles is Pacific Time (UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 daylight). Berlin is Central European Time (UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 daylight). So difference is 9 hours during standard time (Los Angeles behind Berlin by 9 hours). During daylight saving, difference is 9 hours as well? Let's check: In summer, Los Angeles is UTC-7, Berlin is UTC+2, difference is 9 hours. In winter, Los Angeles is UTC-8, Berlin is UTC+1, difference is 9 hours. So always 9 hours difference. But if we consider daylight saving changes at different times, there may be a period where difference is 8 or 10 hours. Actually, daylight saving starts/ends at different dates: In US, DST starts second Sunday in March, ends first Sunday in November. In Europe, DST starts last Sunday in March, ends last Sunday in October. So there is a period from early March to late March where difference is 8 hours? Let's calculate: Suppose early March before second Sunday: Los Angeles still on PST (UTC-8), Berlin on CET (UTC+1) until last Sunday in March. So difference is 9 hours. After second Sunday in March, Los Angeles moves to PDT (UTC-7). Berlin remains on CET until last Sunday in March. So difference becomes 8 hours. Then after last Sunday in March, Berlin moves to CEST (UTC+2). Los Angeles is on PDT (UTC-7). Difference becomes 9 hours again. Similarly, in fall: Berlin moves back to CET (UTC+1) on last Sunday in October; Los Angeles remains on PDT until first Sunday in November. So difference becomes 8 hours. Then after first Sunday in November, Los Angeles moves back to PST (UTC-8); Berlin is on CET (UTC+1). Difference becomes 9 hours again.

Thus, difference is usually 9 hours but can be 8 hours for a few weeks each year. The user likely expects a simple answer: 9 hours. But we could mention the daylight saving differences.
